title: Neoadjuvant Porustobart with Pembrolizumab in Resectable pMMR/MSS Colon Cancer
official: A Phase 2, Open-Label, Multicenter, Randomized Trial Evaluating the Efficacy and Safety of Different Schedules of Neoadjuvant Pembrolizumab and Porustobart in Patients with Resectable pMMR/MSS Colon Cancer (SOL1-201)
summary: Main objective: To assess the major pathologic response (MPR) rate by BIPR (blinded independent pathologic review) in each arm.
conditions: Resectable proficient mismatch repair (pMMR) / microsatellite stable (MSS) colon cancer

interventions.name: KEYTRUDA 25 mg/mL concentrate for solution for infusion

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. 1. Capable and willing to provide a signed and dated written informed consent obtained before the performance of any protocol-related procedures that are not part of normal patient care.
2. 2. ≥18 years of age at the time of consent
3. 3. Adenocarcinoma of the colon (and rectosigmoid considered as non-rectal): a. MMR/MSS status as determined through local testing by one of the following: i. pMMR: immunohistochemistry (IHC) measurement of mismatch repair proteins MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2 where presence of all 4 indicate pMMR ii. non-MSI-H (referred to as MSS in protocol): PCR or NGS measurement where there are no increases in microsatellite repeats or length indicative of an intact repair mechanism b. Any T3 or T4, Nx, M0  c. Disease considered amenable for surgical resection as per treatment team
4. 4. ECOG Performance Status 0-1
5. 5. A sufficient and adequate tumor tissue sample (formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded [FFPE] block or 10 unstained slides, defined in the Laboratory Manual) that is available and planned to provide along with an associated pathology report.  a. The tumor tissue sample may be fresh or archival if obtained within 3 months prior to consent. b. Tissue must be a core needle biopsy, excisional or incisional biopsy by endoscopy (e.g., snare). Fine needle biopsies obtained by endobronchial ultrasound are not considered adequate. c. Tissue must be provided with an associated pathology report.
6. 6. Adequate organ and bone marrow reserve function, as indicated by the following laboratory values:  a. Adequate hematological function, defined as absolute neutrophil count (ANC) ≥1.5 × 10^9 /L, platelet count ≥100 × 10^9/L, and hemoglobin levels of ≥8 g/dL (transfusion permitted)   b. Adequate liver function, defined as total bilirubin level ≤1.5 × upper limit of normal (ULN) (except for patients with Gilbert syndrome who must have a total bilirubin level of ≤3.0 × ULN), aspartate aminotransferase (AST) ≤2.5 × ULN, and alanine aminotransferase (ALT)  ≤ 2.5 × ULN. c. Adequate renal function, defined as calculated creatinine clearance ≥40 mL/min as determined by the Cockcroft-Gault equation.
7. 7. Must meet the requirements for reproductive status as defined below:  a. Women of childbearing potential (WOCBP) must:  a. Not be breastfeeding  b. Have a negative serum or urine pregnancy test (minimum sensitivity of 25 IU/L or equivalent units of human chorionic gonadotropin [hCG]) within 72 hours prior to the start of study treatment.  c. Agree to follow instructions for method(s) of contraception  and not donate eggs for the duration of treatment with pembrolizumab and 5 months after the last dose of study treatment (i.e., 30 days [duration of ovulatory cycle]) plus the time required for the investigational drug to undergo approximately 5 half-lives. d. WOCBP who are continuously not heterosexually active are exempt from contraceptive requirements, but still must undergo pregnancy testing as described in this section.   b.  Males who are sexually active with WOCBP must agree to follow instructions for method(s) of contraception  for the duration of treatment with pembrolizumab and 7 months after the last dose of study treatment (i.e., 90 days [duration of sperm turnover] plus the time required for the investigational drug to undergo approximately 5 half-lives). In addition, male patients must be willing to refrain from sperm donation during this time.  a.  Azoospermic males are exempt from contraceptive requirements.
Exclusion criteria:
1. 1. Currently participating in a study or has participated in a study of an investigational agent within 3 weeks of the first dose of current study drug.
2. 7. Clinically significant (i.e., active) cardiovascular disease: cerebral vascular accident/stroke or myocardial infarction within 6 months of enrollment, unstable angina, congestive heart failure (New York Heart Association class ≥ II), or serious uncontrolled cardiac arrhythmia requiring medication that may prevent surgery
3. 8. Major surgery within 4 weeks prior to the first dose of study drug
4. 9. Active infection requiring treatment.
5. 13. Prior malignancy active within the previous 3 years except for locally curable cancers that have been apparently cured, such as basal or squamous cell skin cancer, superficial bladder cancer, or carcinoma in situ of the prostate, cervix, or breast or with a negligible recurrence rate (e.g., <10% in 5 years)
6. 14. Patients with serious or uncontrolled medical disorders not otherwise defined above
7. 15. Psychiatric or substance abuse disorder that would interfere with cooperation with the requirements of the study
8. 16. Legally incapacitated or has limited legal capacity
9. 10. Patients with active hepatitis B (positive hepatitis B surface antigen [HBsAg]) or hepatitis C virus ([HCV]-positive HCV RNA) with the following caveats: a. Patients with past HBV infection or resolved HBV infection (defined as the presence of hepatitis B core antibody [HBcAb] and the absence of HBsAg) are eligible. HBV DNA must be obtained in these patients prior to randomization.  b. HBV carriers or those patients requiring antiviral therapy are not eligible to participate. c. Patients who are positive for HCV antibody are eligible only if polymerase chain reaction is negative for HCV RNA.
10. 11. Known positive test for human immunodeficiency virus-1 antibody (HIV-1 Ab) or human immunodeficiency virus-2 antibody (HIV-2 Ab) unless the patient is wellcontrolled with highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART) and CD4+ cell count >350/uL and viral load is undetectable
11. 12. Live vaccination within 28 days prior to receiving the first dose of immunotherapy
12. 2. Imminent or urgent need for surgery (e.g., risk of perforation)
13. 3. Prior systemic anticancer therapy (including chemotherapy, targeted therapy, or immunotherapy) or radiotherapy for colon cancer or any prior treatment with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) targeting cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-associated protein 4 (CTLA-4), programmed cell death protein-1 (PD-1), or programmed cell death protein ligand-1 (PD-L1)
14. 4. Receiving systemic corticosteroid therapy or other forms of systemic immunosuppressivemedication 1 week prior to the first dose of study drug. Corticosteroid use as a premedication for IV contrast allergies/reactions is permitted. Patients who receive daily corticosteroid replacement therapy (prednisone at doses of ≤10 mg or equivalent) are permitted. Use of inhaled or topical corticosteroids is permitted.
15. 5. History of:  a. Severe (Grade ≥3) hypersensitivity reaction to a fully human mAb b. History of interstitial lung disease or lung disease which may interfere with the assessment of pneumonitis c. Pneumonitis that required oral or IV corticosteroids
16. 6. Active or history of autoimmune disease that required systemic treatment within 2 years of the start of study drug (i.e., with use of disease-modifying agents, corticosteroids, or immunosuppressive drugs). Patients with autoimmune conditions requiring hormone  replacement therapy or topical treatments are eligible.
